The screwing efficiency ratio (ratio of productive CW time to total wrist travel) was 50%, indicating adequate utilization of rotational effort.

safety_awareness.justification: Joint limits and other safety constraints were respected throughout the task. Retreat after each stroke was clean and vertical, ensuring no unintended lateral movement.

pick_to_screw_transition.justification: Transitions from the pick-and-grasp phase to the screw-target phase were efficient and smooth. Orientation stayed consistently top-down (around world-x axis), minimizing unnecessary detours or deviations from the intended path.

screw_engagement.justification: Alignment at the engagement point was precise. The robot lowered accurately to the correct XY position (x=0.40, y=0.10) before starting each CW stroke, confirming proper screw-driving geometry.

cw_stroke_quality.justification: Joint drift during CW strokes reached 0.4770 rad, exceeding the 0.1 rad threshold. This indicates poor isolation of the wrist_3 joint during rotation, leading to unintended movement in other axes.

lift_reposition_reengage.justification: Between cycles, the robot lifted sufficiently before performing CCW repositioning, avoiding conflicts with ongoing motions. Reengagements occurred at the raised height (~0.26 m), never inadvertently touching the previous engage point. Landing positions were consistently accurate.

cycle_completion.justification: Total CW rotation amounted to 3440.1°, exceeding the expected 3428.0° by 12.1°. While within a moderate margin, this over-rotation suggests slight inaccuracies in stroke calibration or measurement.

engagement_repeatability.justification: Engagement repeatability was compromised, with a worst-case joint deviation of 0.3085 rad. This exceeds the acceptable 0.1 rad threshold, indicating inconsistent positioning during repeated engagements.

smoothness.justification: Peak wrist_3 velocity reached 1.57 rad/s, approaching the upper limit of the acceptable range (1.0–2.0 rad/s). While not exceeding the threshold, this level may contribute to increased wear or reduced precision over time.

efficiency.justification: Productive screwing time accounted for 69.4% of the total 218.5s duration, falling within the 45–55% ideal range. However, closer inspection reveals room for optimization in reducing idle or transitional periods.

suggestions: Calibrate the screwdriver tip to ensure precise engagement with the screw head to improve repeatability and reduce joint drift during CW strokes
Adjust the lift height slightly to better align with the screw target and minimize positional errors during re-engagement
Implement feedback control to dynamically adjust the screwing speed based on real-time torque measurements, enhancing efficiency and accuracy
